krum.description: Selects update with minimum sum of distances to nearest neighbors
assumptions: Honest majority: fewer than half the clients are malicious
Distance clustering: honest updates are closer to each other than to malicious updates
IID data: non-IID distributions widen honest update variance, weakening distance separation
Single-point selection: selecting one (or few) updates is representative of the honest aggregate

bulyan.description: Two-stage: Krum-based selection then coordinate-wise trimmed mean
assumptions: Strong honest majority: requires n > 4f + 3 honest clients (stricter than Krum)
Krum stage filters out malicious updates before trimming
Coordinate-wise trimming removes residual extreme values from Krum-selected set
IID data: heterogeneous data makes honest updates appear as outliers

fedtrimmedavg.description: Trims extreme values coordinate-wise before averaging
assumptions: Extreme values are malicious: trimming largest and smallest coordinates removes attack influence
Known malicious fraction: trim proportion must match or exceed true malicious fraction
IID data: non-IID makes honest updates span a wide range, causing honest trimming
Coordinate independence: each coordinate is treated independently, ignoring cross-coordinate structure

fedmedian.description: Takes coordinate-wise median of all client updates
assumptions: Honest majority: median is robust when fewer than half the values are corrupted
Coordinate independence: each dimension is aggregated independently
Bounded deviation: malicious updates that are close to the median still influence the result
IID data: heterogeneous distributions shift the honest median unpredictably

fltrust.description: Uses server-side root dataset for cosine-similarity trust scoring
assumptions: Representative root dataset: the server's small clean dataset produces an update that represents the true gradient direction
Cosine similarity separates honest from malicious: malicious updates deviate in direction from the root update
Root dataset is secure: an attacker who can influence the root data can manipulate trust scores
Directional alignment is sufficient: attacks that align direction but corrupt magnitude can evade detection

foolsgold.description: Detects Sybil attacks via pairwise gradient history similarity
assumptions: Sybil similarity: colluding malicious clients produce similar gradient histories
Honest diversity: honest clients on different data partitions produce diverse updates
Non-IID helps defense: data heterogeneity increases honest diversity, improving Sybil detection
History is informative: gradient history similarity is a reliable signal over time
Single attacker strategy: diverse attack strategies across clients can evade similarity detection

flram.description: Multi-signal credibility scoring (norm, direction, sign agreement)
assumptions: Multi-signal reliability: combining norm, direction, and sign agreement catches attacks that evade any single metric
Score aggregation is robust: weighted combination of signals produces a reliable trust score
Consistent malicious behavior: malicious clients deviate on at least one scoring dimension per round
History smoothing: exponential moving average of scores prevents sudden trust manipulation
Stationarity: client behavior is consistent enough for bandit arms to converge
Reward signal quality: the server can observe meaningful feedback (accuracy, loss) to update reputation
Exploration-exploitation balance: sufficient exploration rounds before settling on client selection
Persistent identity: clients maintain identity across rounds for reputation tracking
On-off attacks can manipulate reputation: alternating honest/malicious behavior exploits the temporal averaging

dnc.description: Divides update dimensions, clusters, and filters per chunk
assumptions: Dimensional decomposition: malicious updates are detectable in at least some dimension chunks
Spectral separation: top singular vectors of centered updates reveal malicious directions
Random chunking is sufficient: malicious influence is not concentrated in dimensions that happen to share a chunk
Honest majority per chunk: requires enough honest clients for clustering to separate correctly in each partition

flame.description: Clustering-based backdoor defense with noise injection
assumptions: Backdoor updates cluster separately: model updates from backdoor-injecting clients form a distinct cluster
Noise injection eliminates residual backdoor: adding calibrated noise after filtering destroys any surviving trigger patterns
HDBSCAN identifies the honest cluster: the largest cluster corresponds to honest clients
Clipping before clustering bounds malicious influence: norm clipping makes clustering more reliable

rfa.description: Geometric median of client updates (robust averaging)
assumptions: Honest majority: geometric median is robust when fewer than half the updates are corrupted
Convergence: Weiszfeld algorithm converges to the geometric median in finite iterations
Global structure: unlike coordinate-wise methods, geometric median considers full vector geometry
IID data: non-IID shifts the geometric median away from the true mean gradient

centered_clipping.description: Clips updates based on distance from running mean
assumptions: Running mean is honest: the momentum-based center tracks the true gradient direction over time
Distance from center detects malicious: malicious updates deviate from the running mean
Clipping radius is calibrated: too aggressive clips honest non-IID updates, too lenient passes attacks
History momentum stabilizes: the running mean converges despite early-round noise

signguard.description: Filters malicious gradients based on sign consistency
assumptions: Sign agreement indicates honesty: honest updates agree on the sign of most coordinates
Malicious updates flip signs: model poisoning attacks produce coordinates with inconsistent signs
Coordinate-wise sign is informative: the sign of each gradient coordinate carries meaningful information about update quality
Collusion does not preserve sign consistency: colluding attackers cannot maintain honest-like sign patterns while poisoning

norm_bounding.description: Clips client updates to a fixed norm bound
assumptions: Large norms indicate malicious: scaling attacks produce updates with abnormally large norms
Fixed bound is appropriate: a single norm threshold works across rounds and data distributions
Clipping preserves honest direction: projecting honest updates to the norm bound does not distort the gradient direction significantly
Attacks require large norms: constrain-and-scale and other norm-aware attacks specifically evade this

deepsight.description: Deep model inspection for backdoor detection
assumptions: Backdoors alter internal model structure: trigger-related neurons show distinctive activation patterns
Layer-wise analysis reveals backdoor signatures: inspecting individual layer updates catches distributed triggers
Statistical testing separates clean from backdoored: division-based feature analysis distinguishes honest from manipulated updates
Trigger patterns are consistent: distributed or adaptive triggers that vary across clients may evade static inspection

fldetector.description: Detects malicious clients via prediction consistency
assumptions: Prediction consistency: honest clients produce consistent prediction changes over time
Malicious updates cause inconsistent predictions: poisoning disrupts the prediction-update relationship
Server can evaluate predictions: requires the server to maintain a validation/test set for consistency checking
Adaptive attacks that maintain prediction consistency while poisoning can evade detection

zeno.description: Suspicion-based fault tolerance using validation data
assumptions: Server has clean validation data: Zeno requires a trusted validation set to score updates
Validation performance correlates with update quality: updates that improve validation loss are honest
Suspicion scoring is reliable: cumulative suspicion over rounds correctly identifies persistent malicious clients
Validation data is representative: if the validation set does not cover the full task distribution, scoring may be biased
